text: David asked, "Is there anyone still left of the house of Saul, so that I may show him kindness for Jonathan's sake?"
Now there was a servant of Saul's household named Ziba, and they summoned him to David. The king said to him, "Are you Ziba?" "At your service," he answered.
The king asked, "Is there no one at all left of Saul's house to whom I may show God's own kindness?" Ziba answered the king, "There is still a son of Jonathan; he is crippled in both feet."
"Where is he?" the king asked. Ziba answered, "He is in the house of Machir son of Ammiel, in Lo Debar."
So King David sent and had him brought from the house of Machir son of Ammiel in Lo Debar.
When Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, he fell facedown and bowed low. David said, "Mephibosheth!" "I am your servant," he answered.

versions.text: When Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, he fell facedown in homage. David said, "Mephibosheth!" "I am your servant," he answered.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has two distinct actions, falling on his face and bowing down. "In homage" is an abstract noun that reads stiffly aloud; "fell facedown and bowed low" keeps both verbs and flows better in oral reading.

text: "Do not be afraid," David said to him, "for I will surely show you kindness for the sake of your father Jonathan. I will restore to you all the land that belonged to Saul your grandfather, and you will always eat at my table."

versions.text: "Do not be afraid," David said to him, "for I will surely show you kindness for the sake of your father Jonathan. I will restore to you all the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul, and you will always eat at my table."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads literally "Saul your father," using 'father' in the wider sense of ancestor. Rendering it "Saul your grandfather" keeps the clarification while preserving the name-first word order of the Hebrew; a footnote noting "Hebrew: your father" would also be helpful for readers.

text: Mephibosheth bowed down and said, "What is your servant, that you should notice a dead dog like me?"
Then the king summoned Ziba, Saul's steward, and said to him, "I have given to your master's grandson everything that belonged to Saul and his whole house.

You and your sons and your servants are to farm the land for him and bring in the harvest, so that your master's grandson may have food to eat. And Mephibosheth, your master's grandson, will always eat at my table." (Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.)

versions.text: You and your sons and your servants are to farm the land for him and bring in the harvest, so that your master's grandson may be provided for. And Mephibosheth, your master's grandson, will always eat at my table." (Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.)
versions.explanation: The Hebrew specifies bread/food that he may eat (לֶחֶם וַאֲכָלוֹ). "May be provided for" is vague and loses the concrete idea of food; "may have food to eat" is both accurate and natural to read aloud.

text: Ziba said to the king, "Whatever my lord the king commands his servant, your servant will do." So Mephibosheth ate at David's table like one of the king's sons. [Footnote: Hebrew reads "my table"; the sense is the king's table.]

versions.text: Ziba said to the king, "Whatever my lord the king commands his servant, your servant will do." So Mephibosheth ate at David's table like one of the king's sons.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew text has "my table," which is unexpected on Ziba's lips; the rendering "David's table" is a reasonable reading, but a brief footnote alerting the reader to the Hebrew wording adds transparency without disturbing the oral flow.

text: Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica, and all the members of Ziba's household were servants of Mephibosheth.
So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, and he always ate at the king's table. He was lame in both feet.
